task.description: Re-check ELIXIR-DEV's rework2 fix (commit f14e6eb5) of the two real Postgres-verified defects TEST-DESIGNER found while running its suite: a duplicate/over-length Ecto-default index name on artifact_versions (42P07-class collision + silent NAMEDATALEN truncation), and the resulting mismatch between the truncated real unique-constraint name and ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 name, which let a raw Ecto.ConstraintError escape instead of being caught by the concurrency-retry contract (design §4.4).
acceptance_criteria: Both indexes on artifact_versions have explicit, distinct, <63-byte names
ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 name matches the migration's explicit unique-index name character for character

Every other FK/index name in the migration (content_hash FK, parent_version_id self-FK, plain content_hash index) is independently confirmed under Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit, not just trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's claim
The fix commit changes nothing beyond the naming fix (no incidental behavior change)
Real mix test run against Postgres for the affected test files passes

result.summary:
Read the current state of both files (not the pre-fix version). Migration (priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs, lines 113-138): unique_index/3 on [:artifact_kind, :artifact_name, :version_number] now carries name: :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_idx (38 bytes), and index/3 on [:artifact_kind, :artifact_name, desc: :version_number] now carries name: :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_desc_idx (43 bytes). Both are explicit, distinct from each other, and well under the 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit -- computed length independently (Python len()), not read from a comment.

ArtifactVersion.changeset/2 (lib/letflow/repository/artifact_version.ex:104): @unique_version_number_constraint_name is now :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_idx -- byte-for-byte identical to the migration's new unique_index name. Confirmed by direct string comparison, not inspection alone.

Independently audited every other FK/index name in the migration that ELIXIR-DEV's commit message claimed was already safe (I did not trust the claim -- computed each length myself):
  - content_hash FK default name (references/4 on repository_artifacts, table+column convention): artifact_versions_content_hash_fkey = 35 bytes -- safe.
  - parent_version_id self-FK default name: artifact_versions_parent_version_id_fkey = 40 bytes -- safe.
  - plain content_hash index default name (create index(:artifact_versions, [:content_hash], ...), migration line 138, name left implicit): artifact_versions_content_hash_index = 36 bytes -- safe.
  - For contrast, confirmed the OLD pre-fix default name both changed indexes would have collided on: artifact_versions_artifact_kind_artifact_name_version_number_index = 66 bytes -- over the limit, matching the diagnosis in both ELIXIR-DEV's commit message and the migration's own new comment.
All four independently-computed lengths match the migration's inline reasoning comment (lines 113-123) exactly; no discrepancy found.

Diff audit: `git show f14e6eb5 -- priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs lib/letflow/repository/artifact_version.ex` shows the change is exactly: (1) two new `name:` keyword args added to the existing unique_index/3 and index/3 calls plus a new explanatory comment block, (2) the @unique_version_number_constraint_name atom literal changed and its comment expanded. No table/column/type/on_delete/trigger/timestamps change, no other line touched. Confirmed spec-only-equivalent (naming-only) fix, no incidental behavior change.

Ran the real test suite myself against real Postgres (sourced ~/.asdf/asdf.sh first, did not reuse ELIXIR-DEV's quoted output): `mix test test/letflow/repository_test.exs test/letflow/repository/canonicaliser_test.exs` -> `Finished in 15.1 seconds (0.6s async, 14.5s sync)` / `Result: 38 passed` / 0 failures. Matches ELIXIR-DEV's claimed 38/0 exactly, independently reproduced.

All acceptance criteria met. This was a narrow, mechanical naming-only fix -- prior Step 2d idiom/scope/decision-consistency review from step-02d-reviewer.json and its recheck1 still stands and was not re-litigated here. PASS -- gate cleared. Since TEST-DESIGNER's existing test suite (step-03-test-designer.json) already exists and now passes in full against the fixed code, Step 3 does not need to redo work; routing directly to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b) to validate that suite's coverage.

findings.idiomatic: Explicit, short, distinct index names given via the `name:` option on unique_index/3 and index/3 is the standard idiomatic Ecto fix for NAMEDATALEN collisions -- no crutch pattern; no gen_statem/OTP surface touched by this fix (migration + Ecto schema module only).
findings.supervision: Not applicable -- migration and Ecto schema module, no process/supervision tree involved.
findings.type_safety_gaps: None new. This fix doesn't touch a class of previously-unrepresentable invalid state; the underlying issue was a naming/identifier-length mismatch between two independent sources of truth (migration DDL and changeset constraint name), not a missing type. No new issue filed.
findings.scope_creep: None -- the fix is exactly the two index names plus the matching constraint-name atom; nothing else in the migration or schema was touched, confirmed via git show.

result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b) for REQ-202 -- validate coverage of the existing, now-passing test suite from step-03-test-designer.json.
